summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 45 of the cipher-box project — a Rust-only hygiene refactor of the FUSE write-journal/replay code with 7 scope items and no behavior change.
summary.outcome: Phase 45 was fully planned (6 plans, 5 waves), executed (266 tests passing, 7/7 must-haves verified), and code-reviewed (deep pass, 2 blockers investigated and confirmed false positives). Phase marked complete.

repo: The project uses a GSD workflow system (plan-phase → execute-phase → code-review) with subagent orchestration, wave-based parallel execution, and commit-driven artifacts (SUMMARY, VALIDATION, PATTERNS, REVIEW, VERIFICATION md files).
`.planning/config.json` has `auto_advance: true` which normally chains planning directly into execution — the orchestrator paused for user confirmation before auto-advancing.
The crate is `cipherbox-fuse` (default feature `fuse`); workspace also contains `cipherbox-sdk` and Windows-only crates (`winfsp-sys`, `windows_core`) that cannot build on macOS.

`publish_file_metadata` at operations.rs:125 pre-existed Phase 45 with conflict-swallowing behavior (`Conflict => log::warn + record_publish + Ok`) and was already called by the live release path — the refactor in 45-05 was safe because it matched pre-existing semantics.
The pre-refactor inline replay per-file publish had identical conflict handling to `publish_file_metadata` (warn + continue), making 45-05's replacement a true no-op refactor.
fuser/winfsp `write_generation` asymmetry (fuser bumps it, winfsp doesn't) is pre-existing platform design, not introduced in Phase 45.
The `fuse/windows/mod.rs` had a third undocumented duplicate of the journal-dir helper beyond the two in the plan — discovered and fixed during 45-02 execution.
The gsd-tools commit helper can return false-negative `commit_failed` even on success (a known issue); `git log` is the reliable verification source.

code.finding: publish_file_metadata pre-existed Phase 45 with conflict-swallowing behavior; already called by live release path, making 45-05 reuse semantically safe.
write_generation += 1 bump location post-refactor (was line 297 pre-refactor); still correctly paired with write_gen read into UploadComplete at line 902 (was 957).
IDE showed E0308 at this line after 45-06; confirmed stale rust-analyzer cache — cargo check --workspace exited 0 and 44 tests passed.
New module linked via `pub mod journal_helpers;` in lib.rs; both fuser (read_ops.rs, write_ops.rs) and winfsp (platform/windows/write_ops.rs) use the shared builders after 45-06.

workflow: IDE diagnostics (rust-analyzer) frequently showed stale E0308/type errors after executor commits mid-edit; `cargo check --workspace` is the authoritative ground truth and should always be the verification source, not IDE panels.

Sequential execution on the feature branch is preferable to worktrees when multiple waves serialize through the same file (lib.rs here) — worktree merge machinery adds risk with no parallelism benefit.

Code review agents can produce false-positive blockers when reasoning from partial diff context; orchestrator should cross-check claimed regressions against pre/post code for 'no behavior change' phases.

For cross-platform code with Windows-only deps, macOS hosts cannot verify winfsp paths — Windows CI is the real gate and should be explicitly noted rather than treating the macOS failure as a code defect.

When an executor subagent returns a thin summary without test/check confirmations on a risky refactor, the orchestrator should independently run cargo check and the test suite before marking the plan complete.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper returned false-negative `commit_failed` on successful commits, requiring git log verification after every commit to confirm landing.
rust-analyzer repeatedly cached stale E0308 errors from executor mid-edit state across multiple plans (45-03, 45-06), creating false alarms that required cargo check verification each time.
Plan 45-06 executor returned a thin summary with no test/check confirmations on the riskiest refactor, forcing the orchestrator to run independent verification.

Deep code review produced 2 false-positive blocker findings (CR-01, CR-02) that required significant investigation (reading pre-refactor git history, tracing conflict-handling logic) before they could be dismissed.
winfsp cross-check unavoidably fails on macOS due to Windows-only dependency crates — no way to verify the winfsp execution path locally, creating uncertainty about cross-platform correctness.
open_items: Windows CI is the real correctness gate for the journal_helpers.rs consolidation (45-06) winfsp path — macOS cannot verify this.
Security enforcement is on but no SECURITY.md was created during this phase; a reminder was surfaced in the code review but not acted on.
Pre-existing dead-code warnings in the vendored `fuse_abi.rs` file were noted but left unaddressed (out of scope for this refactor phase).
WR-03: The IpnsResolveOutcome classifier now matches both `'not found'` and `'404'` — the `'404'` addition is a benign superset but the intent could be documented more explicitly.
